title: Advancing Entropy-Level Credit Assignment in RLVR via Proximal Entropy Policy Optimization
claim: Our method reaches higher accuracy and stays stable through training, while the baseline peaks early and then degrades, across model scales.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, starred peaks with dotted reference lines
description: Two side-by-side line charts share the x-axis 'Training Steps' (0 to about 480) and the y-axis 'Mean Accuracy (%)'. Panel (a) is Qwen3-1.7B and panel (b) is Qwen3-4B. Each panel has a purple line for PEPO (Ours) and a blue line for the 80/20 baseline, each with a translucent shaded band for variance. Star markers show each curve's peak, with dotted horizontal lines and large bold labels in matching colors: 45.20 vs 42.83 in (a), 57.61 vs 55.33 in (b). The curves rise together early. The blue baseline then plateaus and declines, with a wide noisy band, while the purple curve keeps climbing and stays higher. A legend box sits at the bottom right of each panel. The eye goes first to the peak labels and the gap between the curves.
caption: Validation accuracy over training steps for PEPO and the 80/20. The plotted values represent the average mean@k accuracy evaluated across the MATH, AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and AMC benchmarks for Qwen3-1.7B (a) and Qwen3-4B (b). PEPO achieves a higher validation accuracy compared to the 80/20 baseline.
abstract: Value-model-free RLVR methods such as GRPO assign uniform advantages to all tokens in a rollout, ignoring that tokens contribute unequally. Recent methods use token entropy as an importance proxy but compute it globally across the batch, conflating importance with prompt difficulty and positional trends. We argue that importance should instead be measured relative to the local context of each token. We introduce proximal entropy, a local measure of token importance relative to neighboring tokens, and prove it is invariant to both confounders. Proximal Entropy Policy Optimization (PEPO) uses it to weight per-token advantages and outperforms GRPO and entropy-based baselines on mathematical reasoning across Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct. We also show the formulation generalizes to other algorithms where substituting proximal entropy into existing methods improves, and applying it to single-stream RL succeeds where global entropy fails.
